newsitem.title: USA: KeyCorp cuts 2,700 jobs in restructuring.
newsitem.headline: KeyCorp cuts 2,700 jobs in restructuring.

text.p: KeyCorp said Monday it plans to take a $100 million charge and eliminate 2,700 jobs, or about 10 percent of its work force, as it consolidates its 12-bank network into a single nationwide bank.

The company, which currently operates 12 banks in 14 states, also said that as part of the restructuring it plans to sell more than 140 of its branch offices, known as KeyCenters, primarily in rural areas, leaving about 1,000.

KeyCorp, which has about $65 billion in assets, said it will take the $100 million charge in the fourth quarter but expected to realise about $110 million in annualized earnings benefits by the end of next year.

The Cleveland-based company, which has about 1,400 offices in 44 states, also said its board authorised a new share buyback programme, effective immediately, in which up to 12 million shares may be repurchased by the end of 1997.

KeyCorp said the new bank will emphasise community and corporate banking products and services and will complement the delivery of consumer finance products through KeyBank USA, which will remain as a separate company.
"These are bold steps that will complete the process we launched 18 months ago to transform Key into a nationwide financial services provider," Chairman Robert W. Gillespie said in a statement.
"These actions will accelerate our schedule for completion of these tasks and position Key among the top-performing financial services companies in terms of both productivity and earnings growth."
KeyCorp said the work force reductions will be distributed throughout the company and its regions and be represented in all job levels.
Affected employees will be eligible for other open positions within the company or be offered separation assistance, it said.
KeyCorp's stock, which closed Friday at $48.875, did not immediately begin trading when the New York Stock Exchange opened Monday.
